archetypes.name: Disturbed Ground of Unknown Safety & Industrial Debris
visual_markers: Dark, oily, or unnatural stains on ground
Rusted scrap metal, wire, or shattered masonry
Irregular, patchy weed clumps with bare dead zones
Remnants of collapsed walls or old foundations
smell_markers: Chemical, fuel, solvent, or sharp metallic odor
tactile_markers: Greasy or gummy texture that leaves dark film on skin
Embedded sharp gravel, glass, and slag
inherent_risks: Heavy metal accumulation (lead from paints/fuels, arsenic, cadmium)
Severe compaction and anaerobic dead zones
safety_rules: STRICT VETO: Do NOT grow root crops (potatoes, carrots, beets) in raw ground.
STRICT VETO: Do NOT consume wild plants growing directly in stained patches.
MANDATORY REMEDY: Physical isolation barrier + knee-high raised beds with imported clean leaf-mold/compost.

archetypes.name: Demolition Rubble & Mortar Fill
visual_markers: High proportion of crushed concrete, red brick chunks, and gray plaster
Stunted, calciphilic weeds (mullein, wild mustard, dandelions)
smell_markers: Absence of rich forest earth smell
tactile_markers: Gritty, sharp, highly abrasive to bare hands
Resists hand-digging; requires levering scrap metal rods
inherent_risks: Excessive alkalinity (concrete locks out phosphorus and iron)
Hidden asbestos fibers or lead paint flakes in older masonry debris
safety_rules: Clear surface chunks down to forearm depth.
Buffer alkaline dust with deep layers of acid-forming organic matter (rotted pine needles, decaying oak leaves).
Grow alkaline-tolerant top crops (Swiss chard, brassicas) in raised pockets.

archetypes.name: Heavily Compacted Hardpan / Footing Fill
visual_markers: Smooth, hardened surface baked into dry plates
Water pools in shallow muddy puddles for hours after rain
Only deep-taproot survivors (plantain, dandelion, crabgrass) can penetrate
smell_markers: Rotten egg smell if standing water has stagnated underneath
tactile_markers: Stick probe will not penetrate deeper than two finger-widths
Fingernails cannot scratch more than a pinch of dust
inherent_risks: Instant root rot during rain, baked brick during sun
safety_rules: Do NOT till or flip into big clods—it turns to concrete blocks.
Break surface crust with a heavy crowbar or pointed rebar (broadfork motion).
Cover with a knee-high thick blanket of decaying branches and mulch to draw worms.

archetypes.name: Exhausted Silt / Crusted Dead Topsoil
visual_markers: Pale, washed-out tan or bleached gray appearance
Fine cracked geometric mud flats when dry
smell_markers: Dusty, faint earth, devoid of sweet fungal richness
tactile_markers: Powders into fine flour when rubbed between palms dry
Forms a slippery, grease-like slick when wet, with no crumb structure
inherent_risks: Severe nitrogen, phosphorus, and organic carbon depletion
Vulnerable to instant sheet erosion during rainstorms
safety_rules: Safe from industrial toxins, but starved of biological life.
Requires immediate pioneer cover cropping (wild legumes/beans) and green manure.

archetypes.name: Coarse Sand & Leached River/Storm Gravel
visual_markers: Loose grit, rounded pebbles, loose coarse sand grains
No natural weeds except deep creeping brambles or tough wiry grasses
Water sinks immediately without leaving a wet patch
smell_markers: Crisp, river stone, faint clean mineral scent
tactile_markers: Cannot form a ball when squeezed wet; slips effortlessly through fingers
inherent_risks: Nutrient desert: rainwater flushes out all organic matter and minerals within hours
Roots desiccate rapidly under midday heat
safety_rules: Line bottom of planting trenches with clay chunks, thick cardboard, or green boughs to trap water.
Add one bucketful of dense compost/humus per pace to bind moisture.

sensory_diagnostic_tests.name: The Jar Sheen & Settle Test
sensory_diagnostic_tests.tool: Clear glass jar or clean halved plastic bottle filled with clean water
sensory_diagnostic_tests.instructions: Place a handful of soil into the jar. Fill with water, cover with palm, and shake vigorously for 30 heartbeats. Place on flat stone and observe for 100 breaths.

readings.observation: Rainbow sheen or oily film forms on water surface; petrochemical or motor oil odor
readings.meaning: Petrochemical or solvent saturation. Lethal for direct food production.
readings.action: Quarantine soil immediately. Must use barrier isolation + raised beds.

readings.observation: Murky water settles into clean layers (sand at bottom, silt in middle, floating leaves on top), water clears within a few hours
readings.meaning: Healthy natural mineral separation with good organic humus particles.

sensory_diagnostic_tests.what_it_cannot_prove: Does not prove the absence of dissolved clear chemicals, pesticides, or odorless heavy metal salts (lead/cadmium).

sensory_diagnostic_tests.name: The Thumb-Thick Stick Penetration Test
sensory_diagnostic_tests.tool: A straight green branch, thumb-thick, stripped of leaves
sensory_diagnostic_tests.instructions: Hold stick vertically with both hands and lean your upper body weight onto it. Note how deep it sinks before hitting resistance.

readings.observation: Sinks less than one hand-width (less than 4 finger-widths)
readings.meaning: Severe compaction or buried concrete pan. Plant roots cannot breathe or expand.
readings.action: Must build knee-high raised mounds or mechanically crack open with rebar.

sensory_diagnostic_tests.what_it_cannot_prove: Cannot prove biological fertility or cleanliness of soil; only measures physical porosity.

sensory_diagnostic_tests.name: The Fast-Sprout Canary Bioassay
sensory_diagnostic_tests.tool: Two scrap tin cans or halved plastic bottles, fast-germinating seeds (beans, wild cress, radish)
sensory_diagnostic_tests.instructions: Fill Cup A with site soil. Fill Cup B with reference clean leaf-mold gathered from deep undisturbed forest/woods. Sow 5 seeds in each. Keep moist for 7 suns.

readings.observation: Cup A seeds fail to sprout, or emerge with curled, blackened, or bleached yellow cotyledon leaves compared to Cup B
readings.meaning: Presence of active soil toxins, high salt/lime poisoning, or persistent chemical herbicide residue.
readings.action: Abandon in-ground cultivation. Build barrier-isolated raised beds.

readings.observation: Cup A sprouts grow upright, vibrant green, matching Cup B vigor
readings.meaning: Biological toxicity low enough to support plant cellular growth.

sensory_diagnostic_tests.what_it_cannot_prove: CANNOT PROVE CHEMICAL EDIBILITY: A plant may grow vigorously while bioaccumulating toxic heavy metals (lead, cadmium) inside its tissues. Leafy greens and root crops must still be quarantined if ground history is industrial.

sensory_diagnostic_tests.name: The Palm Squeeze & Ribbon Test
sensory_diagnostic_tests.tool: Your bare hands and a few drops of water
sensory_diagnostic_tests.instructions: Take a walnut-sized lump of soil, moisten until it feels like putty. Knead into a ball, then push between thumb and forefinger to squeeze out a ribbon of uniform thickness.

readings.observation: Crumbles instantly, cannot form a ribbon longer than a fingernail
readings.meaning: Sandy loam or gravelly soil. Needs leaf mold and rotting mulch to retain water.
readings.action: Add two bucketfuls of decomposed organic matter per bed.

readings.observation: Forms a ribbon longer than two thumb-joints that bends without breaking
readings.meaning: Heavy dense clay. High mineral nutrition, but risks waterlogging and cracking.
readings.action: Add coarse grit, crushed charcoal, and dry shredded leaves.

readings.observation: Forms a soft ribbon about one thumb-joint long, feels velvety like moist breadcrumbs

sensory_diagnostic_tests.what_it_cannot_prove: Cannot determine nutrient deficiencies or toxicity levels.

untested_blindspots_warning: CRITICAL SURVIVOR KNOWLEDGE: Household and sensory tests can assess physical structure, compaction, biological life, and gross petrochemical contamination. However, sensory tests CANNOT detect invisible heavy metals (Lead, Arsenic, Cadmium, Mercury) or colorless, odorless industrial toxins. On unknown disturbed or industrial ground, physical barrier isolation is mandatory for human safety.
